source: davidi_kcat.json (Drive) — 592 enzymes, in-vivo kapp = max|v|/[E] over 13 NCI-60 conditions
circularity_note: earlier kcat_flag/kcat_verify used enzyme_records incell_rate_per_s = kcat_invitro*sigma (incell_rates.py:161 -> enzyme_record.py:70); correlating/kcat-bounding against it was circular. This file uses flux-derived kapp with NO kcat input.
verdict: CORRECTED / HONEST NULL. On 148 enzymes with a MEASURED kcat and an INDEPENDENT flux-derived kapp: the flag is WEAK (kapp ≤ kcat only 70%, so 30% of correct kcats would be false-flagged; a 100x-too-slow kcat is caught only 65%), and kapp does NOT predict the kcat value (Spearman +0.08, 92x fold-error ≫ 8.7x noise). This OVERTURNS the earlier kcat_flag/kcat_verify claims (99% flag, 0.93 Spearman), which were CIRCULAR — they used incell_rate = kcat×sigma. The kapp method is real (works in E. coli, r≈0.6), but our human reconstruction uses FBA-PREDICTED flux + a reference proteome, which is too noisy to flag or recover kcat per-enzyme. What survives: flux kapp is a genuine but noisy LOWER-BOUND signal, useful in aggregate, not as a per-enzyme verdict.
